events.text: Very heavy rain produced flooding across large portions of Groves, Nederland, and Port Arthur. Many roads were flooded and impassable while numerous homes flooded.
Heavy rain caused water levels in ditches near China, TX to rise above bank full.
A gauge site on Lawhon Road indicates the creek out of its bank and rising slowly over nearby streets. Street flooding was also reported in Beaumont.
A tree was downed in Fannett.
A wind gust of 61 knots was measured by a KFDM Mesonet.
A wind gust of 56 knots was measured at Utopia Ranch.
Flooding occurred in the Bor-Ley Heights subdivision with at least one home receiving minor flooding.
Washington Blvd near MLK in Downtown Beaumont became impassable. The Crocket Street underpass was also filled to the top.
Numerous streets flooded in Beaumont with cars stalled on North 11th and on the I-10 service road.
Lightning struck a storage tank on Proctor Street starting a blaze that also engulfed a nearby tank.
Multiple streets were flooded in Beaumont with one water level gage reported water just under 2 feet over the roadway near downtown.

Several roads were impassable in Beaumont including the feeder along Hwy 69, Cedar, the intersection of College and MLK, the underpass in Downtown Beaumont, Orleans, and the feeder of I-10 near Babe Zaharias.
Multiple reports of minor street flooding were received from Beaumont.
A flag pole was broken by high winds.
A cold front moved through southeast Texas with thunderstorms developing along the boundary. One storm became severe along the coast before exiting into Louisiana.
A cold front moved through southeast Texas with thunderstorms developing along the boundary. One storm became severe along the coast before exiting into Louisiana.
A weathernet station recorded a wind gust of 83 mph at the Sabine Pass School.

Light snow began during the early morning hours across lower Jefferson County with heavy snow moving in around sunrise. Winds frequently gusted into the 25 to 35 range along the coast while visibilities fell to around 1/4 for multiple hours. Accumulations ranged from 4 to 6 inches.
Light snow began during the early morning hours across upper Jefferson County with heavy snow moving in around sunrise. Accumulations ranged from 3 to 6 inches.
Golf ball size hail was reported at the Pleasure Island RV resort just before winds flipped multiple RVs.

Six RVs were flipped along the west bank of Sabine Lake on Pleasure Island. Two people were injured. This was caused by strong winds flowing into the approaching tornadic supercell that would pass to the south of the RV park.

An EF-3 tornado developed south of Houston and moved across Chambers County into Jefferson County just south of Russel Road. It snapped off power poles at French Rd before continuing northeast. An area of trees were snapped off and uprooted just south of the Big Hill Strategic Oil Reserve. The tornado continued northeast where it destroyed the top floor of the Sabine Ranch Lodge, stripped metal from a nearby industrial building, flipped a car into a side yard, and damaged the roofs of two homes. The car contained two people, one sustained a minor injury. The tornado crossed Highways 87 and 82 where it snapped transmission poles. Finally, it moved overtop Sabine Lake. The track cont…
A stream gage indicated water over Landis Drive southwest of Beaumont. Other locations also received minor flooding during the event with shallow water over roadways on the southside of Beaumont.
Water was reported over several roads just north of Interstate 10 near Hampshire.
Minor street flooding occurred from Beaumont through Central Gardens. Stream gages also indicated bayous and ditches in the area were overflowing.

In lower Jefferson County tides of 2.50 to 3.25 feet MHHW occured at the peak of the event at 8:48 AM CST. Across Jefferson County Texas, most of Highway 87 from Sabine Pass to Sea Rim State Park has water and debris covering the road. At Sea Rim State Park, damage to buildings and entrance roadways occurred due to storm surge of 1 to 2 feet above park grounds.
The highest winds recorded within our area occurred at Sabine Pass, Texas with a maximum sustained wind of 55 mph (48 knots) and a peak wind gust of 70 mph (61 knots) around 11 AM CDT July 8th.

Alberto moved onshore during the 20th of June with tides along the coast of Jefferson County reaching 2 feet or more above MHHW for 2 tide cycles. The water level reached 2.91 feet above MHHW at 1030Z on the 20th at TXPT2. Minor flooding was noted around Sabine Pass.
The gage at Green Pond Road indicated the water had overflowed the ditch and covered the road.
Portions of MLK Parkway were under water along with several side streets.
A report was received of water over roadways in Port Neches.
A wind gust of 51 knots was recorded at PORT2.
A wind gust of 73 mph was recorded on an Ambient Weather Station.
Flooding was reported around Beaumont with portions of 380 closed from high water.
Golf ball to hen egg size hail was reported around Groves.
A report of three quarter to one inch hail was received from Port Arthur.

An upper trough parked over the region for near a week. Short waves kept traversing the base of the trough for the duration of the event causing several days of unsettled weather. Some days produced severe squall lines with numerous reports of damage.
A helicopter was spun around and a boarding stairway was blown down the tarmac. The KBPT ASOS registered a wind gust of 56 mph before the sensor stopped reporting.
Ping pong ball sized hail reported in Fannett.
Several pictures of large hail were received through social media from Hampshire.
Lightning struck a home causing a house fire on Pine Island Road. No injuries were reported.

Multiple roads in Beaumont, Nederland, and Port Neches were closed during a slow moving line of thunderstorms including Highway 380, 347, and 366 and Nall Street. Flooding of several streets were also reported in China and Hampshire. Taylor Bayou also overflowed near Hampshire.
The river gage in Bevil Oaks indicated minor flooding from a thunderstorm.
Heavy rain caused roads on the north side of Beaumont near the Parkdale Mall be be flooded.
Heavy rain flooded underpasses in Beaumont. Twin City Highway flooded through Central Gardens and multiple streets also flooded in Nederland.
A microburst produced high winds at the Jack Brooks Regional Airport. In neighboring portions of Nederland numerous trees and powerlines were also downed.
Several streets flooded around Nederland with a few cars flooded on South 8th Street.
Broadcast media relayed reports of minor damage to commercial buildings along with power poles and lines downed.

A NWS storm survey revealed that an EF-2 tornado impacted areas of Port Arthur. The tornado began near the intersection of 17th Street and Savannah Ave southeast of Motiva. The tornado path traveled east, peaking out near the Progressive Missionary Baptist Church where a large portion of the masonry walls collapsed. Another home near 11th Street and Orange Ave had the roof completely removed and some walls collapsed. Home and tree damage was extensive across these neighborhoods in Port Arthur. The path continued across Rose Hill Park and onto Pleasure Island. The tornado likely continued into Sabine Lake. Maximum estimated winds were 120 mph.
A trailer was overturned due to a high wind gust at the South Texas State Fair at Ford Park.
A photo of half dollar sized hail was receive from near Bevil Oaks.
A tree was downed along 7100 Tram Road in Beaumont.
The gages at the Green Acres Screw Gate and Mayhaw Bayou measured levels consistent with minor flooding from Beaumont to Fannett.
Multiple ditch and stream gages indicated flooding on roadways from Beaumont to Fannett.
A photo of hail was sent in through social media. Most hail was around dime sized however a few quarter sized stones were mixed in.
The south fork of Taylor Bayou flooded roadways near Interstate 10 after heavy rain fell near Hampshire.
A Tempest weather station recorded a wind gust of 63 mph.
A local water level station reported water over the banks. An MPING report also indicated cars flooded near the location. A personal weather station recorded 3.62 inches of rain in one hour.
A KFDM mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 60mph.
Trees and powerlines were downed in Beaumont. One tree fell onto a car on 5th Street.
A wind gust of 68 MPH was recorded at the Pietzsch-Macarthur School by a KFDM mesonet. A building was also damaged at Gladys City.
Streets were briefly flooded by heavy rain in Port Neches.
A large branch was broken off a tree.
A softwood tree was split in half.
One inch hail near Ford Park.
Reported through social media.
Reported through social media.
An MPING report of hail to 1 inch in diameter.
A picture of hail ranging from quarters to golf ball size was received through social media.
Streets were flooded and cars were stalled due to heavy rain.
A large tree was downed onto a roof in Port Acres.
A mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 64 mph.
Power poles were snapped in Beauxart Gardens. Southeast Texas Regional Airport also recorded a wind gust of 55 mph.

An EF-1 tornado touched down just south of Highway 73, and tracked into the Taylor Landing community. Weak damage to roofs were common, along with uprooted trees and destroyed privacy fences. The tornado ended somewhere in the Taylor Bayou marsh downstream from Taylor Landing. Max estimated winds were 90 mph.
Multiple homes suffered damage from high wind gusts.
Stream gages indicated multiple bayous or ditches overflowed in China and Hampshire. Numerous roads were also flooded by several inches of rain in west Jefferson County.
A flagpole was snapped and leaning on a home.
A gulf low develop along the Texas coast and moved northeast across the region. Heavy rain and severe storms occurred ahead of the low and associated cold front.
Heavy rain flooded streets in portions of Groves. Water was reported to be at least 1 foot deep over Twin City Highway near Thomas Jefferson Middle School.

Numerous videos and pictures were received through social media of a slow moving waterspout moving from Sabine Lake into Motiva. The land spout produced no noticeable damage beyond tipping over trash cans.
Multiple streets were flooded with some cars stranded in Port Arthur, Nederland, and Groves. Water also approached some structures in Port Arthur.
KBPT recorded a wind gust of 67 mph.
A few homes had minor roof damage, however one home had the roof destroyed. Numerous trees were downed or had large limbs broken. Fences were also down in the area.
Media reported roof damage to a business in Nederland.
Street flooding was reported in Beaumont with some streets impassable.

A brief tornado started just west of Nick Ave in Port Acres where there was damage to out buildings and caused some roof damage to homes. The tornado moved northeast crossing Silver Ave then curved north northeast crossing 63 street before dissipating near 64th Street. Numerous limbs were blown down. Max estimated winds were 80 MPH.
Multiple streets across Jefferson County were flooded with underpasses closed while Nicholas moved across the region.
Several hours of tropical storm conditions were recorded at the tide gage at Sabine Pass. The highest sustained winds reached 41 knots with the highest wind gust recorded at 54 knots.
A slow moving thunderstorm produced 10 to 16 inches of rain over the Hampshire - Fannett area which flooded numerous homes, businesses, vehicles, and streets.

Heavy rain around Port Arthur and surrounding communities caused numerous roads to be flooded. Water over 3 feet deep was reported at one underpass. Several cars were also reported to be flooded out in Groves.
A heat burst produced strong wind gusts that damaged a garage near Jack Brooks Regional Airport.

Freezing rain moved into the region during the early morning of the 17th. Ice accumulations of up to one tenth of an inch occurred coating the already in place sleet and snow from the event just 2 days prior. This also created more hazardous driving conditions.

Temperatures fell through the afternoon and evening across Jefferson County as showers developed. Rain turned to freezing rain during the evening and then quickly over to sleet. Light snow mixed in by the end of the event. Accumulations ranged from around half an inch on the coast to near 2 inches north of Beaumont. Bridges and overpasses became iced and closed. Most roads were hazardous. A 65 year old man in Labelle died from hypothermia due to exposure.
Multiple RVs were blown over at an RV park. One person suffered minor injuries.
Winds blew down fencing and a utility pole.
A tree was downed on to a home.

As Hurricane Delta moved into Cameron Parish to the west of Sabine Pass winds reached hurricane force along the coast. At Sabine Pass winds became sustained at 70 knots with a gust to 87 knots. Winds were slightly lower inland with a sustained wind of 57 knots and a gust of 78 knots recorded at the Jack Brooks Airport. Rainfall totals ranged from 5 to 6.5 inches across the county. The tide reached 3.12 feet MHHW at Sabine Pass.

Mandatory evacuation. Storm surge flooded Sabine Pass and backed up area waterways including the Neches River, Hillebrandt Bayou, and Taylor Bayou. Numerous trees and power lines blown down across Port Arthur, Port Neches, Beaumont, Nederland, and Groves. Homes and businesses were damaged by the fallen trees, lines, and poles. Over 60 percent of the county was without power during the peak of the storm. Five people died (indirect deaths) from carbon monoxide poisoning including three in Port Arthur from a generator running in an enclosed area. Another 18 persons were injured and treated for carbon monoxide poisoning (indirect injuries). Wind gusts ranged from 55 to 90 mph across th…
The public and local media reported damage to an aluminum carport, the roof at Grand Slam Carwash on College and 23rd, and multiple trees down in the area with one landing on a home on Broadway.
KBMT 12 relayed a report of trees downed near China.
A construction worker was building an outdoor kitchen in the Diamond D Ranch Subdivision near China when he was struck by lightning. He was hospitalized for 2 week before passing in early June.

Multiple roads in Beaumont were flooded and closed. Some vehicles in a car dealership were flooded and water approached several homes and businesses. A home rain gauge in the area recorded 5.72 inches during the event.
A cold front drifted into the area and stalled while short waves passed aloft. Severe weather occurred over multiple days with hail, wind damage, and tornadoes reported.
One inch in diameter hail reported via social media.
The ASOS at Jack Brooks Regional Airport (KBPT) recorded a wind gust of 60 kts or 69 mph.

The remnants of Imelda drifted slowly across the interior sections of Southeast Texas during the 18th. A very heavy band of rain dumped over 30 inches of rain in a 12 hour period which created extensive flooding across Jefferson County. The maximum storm total was 44.29 inches near Fannet. The first report of flooding was from the Jefferson County Sheriff's Department with major street flooding in the city of Beaumont and water was entering several homes. Due to the intense rate at which the rain fell flooding depth was worse than Harvey at some locations. Over 5100 homes were flooded. Numerous high water rescues were conducted through out the county. Three people drowned in Jeffer…
A report of flooding along Gulfway Drive and Stadium Road in Port Arthur.
Street flooding was reported in Port Arthur and Port Neches closing some roads.
A video that was posted to the NWS social media page indicated flooding along the EasTex Freeway feeder roads in the north side of Beaumont.
Water flooded portions of MLK Jr Parkway impassable near Lamar. Underpasses were flooding on the roadway.
Personal weather station recorded a wind gust of 60 mph in groves.
KBPT ASOS recorded a wind gust of 52 knots.
A dock crane was blown over into the Neches Ship Channel. A large salvage crane also broke loose.
Tree branches around 3 inches thick and power poles were broken in Nederland.

South of Fannett, an area of a strong thunderstorms began bowing out leading to an increase in velocities. Tree damage began to become increasingly evident in a width extending from around Boondocks Road south of Fannett to just north of FM 365. Tree damage continued to be noted eastward into parts of Port Arthur, Groves and Nederland as the bow echo continued to fan outward. In this area, wind was estimated to be between around 60-80 MPH as the bow echo moved through. More severe tree damage and some minor outbuilding damage was noted in the community of La Belle and extending eastward along Garner Road where the bow velocities appeared at their maximum.
Minor roof damage was done to a home near Jack Brooks Regional Airport.
A tree was downed by a thunderstorm.
Several large tree limbs were down at a residence in Beaumont.
Multiple trees were downed in the La Belle area.
Several trees were blown down in the Bevil Oaks community some of which damaged homes.
The ASOS at Jack Brooks Regional Airport recorded a 58 MPH wind gust.
A few utility poles were blown down in Beaumont near Ford Park and also in Port Neches. Wind gust were 40 to 45 MPH.
A tree was blown down onto a storage shed on Trinidad Street.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Bevil Oaks.
Multiple streets were flooded during the storm with some impassable. At least 1 vehicle was stalled on Taft AVE.
Pictures from social media indicated a landspout briefly occurred in a rice field 2 miles south of China. No damage was reported.

Numerous roads were closed in Beaumont, Groves, and Port Arthur due to flooding including underpasses which had up to 5 feet of water. Photos also indicated water levels approached some structures. Rainfall reports from DD6 recorded 4 to 8 inches, however radar estimates indicated some areas in the city my have received around 9 inches during the morning.
Multiple videos taken around Port Arthur and Groves indicated a landspout briefly occurred near Sabine Lake and Pleasure Island. No damage was noted.
A home received roof damage from a thunderstorm near the intersection of Bluebonnet and Richmond Avenues in Port Arthur.
Numerous streets were flooded in Port Arthur, Groves, and Central Gardens with several cars reported flooded.
Underpasses flooded along MLK Blvd with at least one car stalled during the heavy rain event where near 8 inches fell.
A report of golf ball size was reported in Beaumont.
Multiple reports of quarter size hail was reported along Major Drive in Beaumont.
A funnel cloud picture was posted on Social Media. The funnel cloud occurred roughly 8 miles west-southwest of Nederland.

At Lamar University, strong winds uplifted and peeled back a large portion of the University Police station and toppled several large trees. A glass wall and several windows were also blown in. On Oregon Ave, the exterior brick wall of an apartment building collapsed. Max estimated wind gusts were between 105 and 110 MPH.

Pictures on social media indicated standing water and stalled cars along Jimmy Johnson Blvd shortly after 6 AM. Heavy rain continued with one rain gauge reporting 10.18 inches in Groves and another reporting 7.68 inches in Hampshire. Many streets were flooded during the event with numerous homes becoming flooded in Port Acres where some were being remodeled from flooding due to Harvey.

A light dusting of snow over a thin glaze of ice occurred during the morning of the 16th. Area travel was interrupted and area schools canceled classes for the day. Interstate 10 through Beaumont was also shut down during the event due to ice on overpasses. KBPT received 0.1 of snow for the day.

One to five inches of snow fell across Jefferson County. The highest amount at 5 inches was received from Fannet. Area bridges became icy and Interstate 10 had some overpasses close. Schools also closed during the event.

Record or near record crests along the Lower Neches River occurred during Tropical Storm Harvey. Areas along the river stayed flooded during much of the first week of September as the Neches remained above major flood stage. This affected some refineries near the river and also some parks, roadways, and residences. The crest finally moved through Sabine Lake during the 3rd.

Record river stages were observed along Pine Island Bayou and the lower Neches during Harvey. This kept lower sections of Jefferson County flooded into early September which included some river side refineries. The high stream flow in the Neches at Beaumont caused an under water natural gas pipeline to rupture. The river also caused a lot of erosion.

Tropical storm conditions occurred for several hours along the coast of Jefferson County. At Texas Point where the highest winds were recorded peak wind gust of 52 knots occurred during the early morning of the 28th but the highest sustained wind of 42 knots was during the morning of the 29th. Lesser winds were recorded elsewhere, however wind gusts of 35 to 50 knots were common near the coast.

The storm surge from Harvey went above 3 feet at Texas Point during the evening of the 27th and fell below 3 feet around mid day on the 28th. The tide peaked at 5.03 feet with a surge of 3.49 feet. Minor beach erosion was noted during the event.

Widespread and long duration rainfall produced a storm total rainfall over 40 inches across a large portion of the county. The highest rainfall totals in Jefferson County were 60.58 inches 1.5 mile southwest of Nederland and 60.54 inches 1.3 mile north of Groves. This resulted in over 64,000 homes being flooded. The hardest hit areas were Port Arthur, Groves, Bevil Oaks, Hamphire, Fannet, China, and northeast Beaumont. Several refineries in the county also received floodwaters and were offline for an extended period. City and county infrastructure was also damaged with water pumps and treatment plants being inundated. Record crests were observed along Pine Island and the lower Nech…
Law enforcement reported water over Old Sour Lake Road.
Heavy rain produced street flooding around Beaumont. Pictures and video were also sent in of flooded Porter and Brooklyn Streets.
Heavy rain produced flooding in Port Arthur. This caused several cars to be stalled on Jimmy Johnson Blvd.
Roof damage from a thunderstorm was reported to a law office and an apartment complex near Central Mall.

The tide at Sabine Pass pushed above 3 feet for multiple hours. The storm tide reached 4.73 feet above MLLW with a surge of 2.99 feet above MLLW. The surge flooded Highway 87 north of Sabine Pass during high tide.
The Jefferson County Sheriff's Department reported street flooding in Beaumont including along Brooks Road.
Quarter size hail was reported between Winnie and Nome.
KBMT relayed a report of quarter size hail near Port Neches.
KBMT relayed a report of trees down at Sul Ross and Williamsburg in the Regina Howell area of Beaumont.
A slow moving upper level disturbance and cold front produced widespread thunderstorms and heavy rain. Some storms became severe and flooding also occurred.
A slow moving upper level disturbance and cold front produced widespread thunderstorms and heavy rain. Some storms became severe and flooding also occurred.
KBMT reports an estimated wind gust of 60 MPH on Major Drive in Beaumont.
A slow moving upper level disturbance and cold front produced widespread thunderstorms and heavy rain. Some storms became severe and flooding also occurred.
A slow moving upper level disturbance and cold front produced widespread thunderstorms and heavy rain. Some storms became severe and flooding also occurred.
Mostly dime size hail, however a few quarters also mixed in during a thunderstorm.
A picture was sent in of a free standing metal tower bent from winds during a thunderstorm.

Broadcast media shared a video of a brief tornado that occurred in a field. The tornado moved roughly half a mile through the field causing no damage. Multiple reports funnel clouds were also received from this storm.
A tree fell and partially damaged 2 homes and a carport and car in North Beaumont. A few other isolated trees were also reported down in the area.
The Jefferson County PD reported a funnel cloud near Fannett. Multiple pictures were also posted to social media.
A wind gust of around 70 MPH was reported with a thunderstorm.
The Beaumont Police Department reported three quarter inch hail.
Beaumont Public Works reported multiple roadways flooded and closed around the city including Westgate Drive and Norwood Drive.
Radar estimated 1 to 6 inches of rain fell around the Hampshire - Fannett area. Pictures posted to social media showed flooded out roadways with water approaching some structures during the event.
Multiple underpasses and streets were flooded and closed in Beaumont.
Multiple trees were downed around Van Buren Elementary and nearby streets in Groves.
TXDOT reported Farm-to-Market 366 AT SH 347 flooded in Jefferson County closing portions of the roads. Over 5 inches of rain was reported during the event by several gauges in the county.
Several pictures of a funnel cloud near Nome were taken and posted to social media.

Heavy rain resulted in flooded streets around the Beaumont area. All underpasses in the city were flooded and closed. Poorly drained roadways like MLK Boulevard near Lamar University was also flooded.
A picture was received through Facebook of hail of half dollar size near Port Arthur.
Closed streets and highways from flooding was reported from Beaumont, Central Gardens, Port Arthur, and Groves.
A picture was received by KBMT of a large cedar tree being split by lightning in Port Neches.

Heavy rain trained across portions of Southeast Texas for multiple hours on already saturated soil. This produced flooding around Beaumont which closed some streets including an underpass along MLK Boulevard and stranded at least one motorist on a feeder road of the Eastex Freeway.
A picture of flooded roadways was received from Beaumont. The image showed water around one foot deep over roadways and becoming impassable.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced heavy rain across Beaumont for a few hours. This combined with already full ditches and wet ground produced street flooding on multiple roadways. Flood waters also approached some homes along Euclid Street, and cars were stalled in under passes near Lamar University.
Beaumont media received multiple photos from along the Eastex Freeway, Delaware Street, Lucas Drive, and other Northeast Beaumont roads that were flooded. Several cars were flooded during the event.
A report was relayed by Beaumont media of penny to quarter sized hail in Nederland.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Port Acres.
One inch in diameter hail was reported in Beaumont.
One inch in diameter hail was reported near Winnie.

Multiple roadways in Jefferson County, but mainly near Nome and Central Gardens were closed after several inches of rain fell during the evening of the 16th. Some of the roadways included in the closure were FM 365, 1406, and 366 along with Highway 347.

Thunderstorms trained across Jefferson County for several hours during the 21st. Jimmy Johnson Blvd, Nall street, and Highway 365 were a few of the streets that were flooded during the event. Numerous reports of cars being stalled due to high water were received as a result of the street flooding.
Lightning struck a home of a Southeast Texas doctor setting the roof on fire. Firefighters were able to extinguish the blaze after a neighbor reported it. No one was injured in the fire.
A funnel cloud was reported along Highway 105 between Beaumont and Sour Lake by Beaumont media.
The Coast Guard station a Sabine Pass reported a funnel cloud around one mile north of the station.
Lightning struck a tree in North Beaumont which then fell on a house damaging the kitchen. Three people were inside the home when the tree fell, but no one was injured.

Heavy rain began during the 17th across Orange and Jefferson Counties with 1 to 5 inches fall before sunrise of the 18th, however during the 18th an additional 4 to 8 inches of rain fell. This large amount of rainfall lead to numerous streets and roadways being flooded including the feeder roads along Interstate 10 between Beaumont and Orange, the Eastex Freeway, MLK Blvd, SH 346, SH 347, and the streets around Lamar Beaumont.
A wind gust of 66 MPH was recorded at the Jack Brooks Regional Airport with a passing severe storm.
A report of large hail was received by the Beaumont Police Department during the afternoon of the 3rd, however the hail size was later determined to be the size of nickels.
A funnel cloud report over Nederland was passed along by Beaumont media.

Temperatures slowly fell to freezing across the northern sections of Jefferson County before sunrise while rain was occurring. This produced around one to two tenths of an inch of ice accumulation along the far northern sections of the county. A very minimal amount of ice occurred near the Beaumont-Port Arthur Regional Airport. No ice related closures were reported, and no ice accumulation occurred along the coast.
Thunderstorms passed across Beaumont producing wind gusts to around 60 MPH along with small hail to pea size.

The event started with light freezing rain with and gradually mixed in with sleet. Ice accumulations during the event were generally under one tenth of an inch with sleet accumulations around half an inch or less. Some area bridges and Interstate 10 briefly closed around Beaumont due to icing.

Freezing rain and flurries moved into the Golden Triangle during the evening of the 23rd with periods of freezing rain occurring through the night and into the next morning. Temperatures at the coast remained above freezing during most of the event with most of the accumulation occurring in middle to northern sections of Jefferson County. Ice accumulation during the event was generally around one tenth of an inch. Interstate 10 was closed as were most bridges in the county.
Several trees and many tree limbs were blown down or broken around Groves. One tree fell on a house.

Heavy rain across the Beaumont area produced flooding along Eastex Freeway from near the Highway 287/69/Interstate 10 spilt to Highway 105 in Beaumont. Flooding caused the exit ramps and frontage roads to be impassable to some cars with lower sitting vehicles flooding.
Nickel sized hail was reported in Bevel Oaks. The small hail lasted for about 8 minutes.
A severe thunderstorm moved southeast across Jefferson County and into Sea Rim State Park producing a wind gust of 57 MPH.
A report was relayed through Facebook of hail mostly nickel sized with some quarter sized mixed in.
Penny sized hail was reported near China via facebook.
Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall caused saturated ground that gave way to flash flooding. Streets and cars were flooded in the north end of Beaumont.

After a wet start to the year more rain fell on the 9th. Slow moving thunderstorms moved into far Southeast Texas and South Louisiana. Flooding was reported across portions of Port Neches with the underpass at Highway 366 and Twin City Highway impassable. One report of 2.73 inches in 3 hours was received from Port Arthur and KBPT received 3.86 inches of rain on the 9th.

Heavy rain across Jefferson and Orange Counties caused many roads to be flooded. Cars were stalled in an underpass in Central Gardens, water approached some homes in Fannet after overflowing the ditches, and many flooded streets were reported around Mauriceville and Bridge City.
The Eastex Freeway service road between East Lucas and Delaware was flooded due heavy rain.
Beaumont Media relayed reports of a funnel cloud near the Southeast Texas Regional Airport. The funnel extended around �� of the way to the ground.

Jefferson county 911 dispatch relayed reports of a funnel cloud near the Rainbow Bridge between Bridge City and Port Arthur. The funnel cloud was associated with a shower moving inland from Sabine Lake.
A public report was received of hail to the size of quarters.
Dime sized hail was reported in Groves and it lasted for about 5 minutes.

A line of storms producing heavy rain slowly moved across Jefferson County producing 4 to 5 inches of rain. Some roadways were noted to have suffered from minor flooding in Beaumont although Park Street near College Street was closed.
The Beaumont Enterprise and KFDM reported Eastex Freeway at East Lucas Drive impassable. Underpasses along MLK Parkway were flooded. Flooding was also reported along Dowlen and Lucas Roads.
An approaching cold front helped produce severe thunderstorms with large hail.
The Port Arthur Transit System was shut down due to widespread street flooding across Port Arthur. One home had water enter it in Port Arthur.

A house that was struck by lightning caught fire in Groves. The fire started in the attic of the two story home, and caused considerable water damage on the first floor and fire damage on the second floor.
Excessive lightning caused a fire at the Stone Hearth Apartments. One unit with eight apartments was on fire and the roof partially collapsed.
A two story home on the west side of Beaumont was struck by lightning. The resulting fire was quickly put out, but not before the home was severely damaged.
Lightning struck a two story house on the west side of Beaumont. The fire quickly spread through the attic, but was put out by firemen who arrived at the scene. No injuries were reported.
An upper level disturbance produced severe thunderstorms in the afternoon across southeast Texas. Wind damage and large hail were reported.
An upper level disturbance produced severe thunderstorms in the afternoon across southeast Texas. Wind damage and large hail were reported.
An upper level disturbance produced severe thunderstorms in the afternoon across southeast Texas. Wind damage and large hail were reported.
An upper level disturbance produced severe thunderstorms in the afternoon across southeast Texas. Wind damage and large hail were reported.
An upper level disturbance produced severe thunderstorms in the afternoon across southeast Texas. Wind damage and large hail were reported.
An upper level disturbance produced severe thunderstorms in the afternoon across southeast Texas. Wind damage and large hail were reported.
Public reported small tree limbs down with an estimated wind gust of 55 mph.
Public reported pea to dime size hail near Lamar University.

A strengthening upper level low over western Texas began to push east-northeast across southeast Texas from the morning of February 3 into February 4. At the surface, temperatures were generally above freezing, but dewpoints were well below freezing. This allowed for a mix of freezing rain, sleet, and snow to develop across southeast Texas during the morning hours of February 3rd, with a changeover to all freezing rain by the afternoon. Freezing rain then continued into the morning of February 4th before ending. Portions of coastal southeast Texas, including the Beaumont/Port Arthur area, received around one tenth of an inch of ice accumulation. Further to the north, most of the La…

The KFDM-TV mesonet measured wind gusts of 45 mph or higher at many stations between 1200 PM CST and 100 PM CST, with a peak wind gust of 53 mph at Lamar University in Beaumont. A TCEQ monitoring station in Port Arthur measured a peak wind gust of 52 mph. The KBPT ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 49 mph at 1218 PM CST. Entergy stated up to 4000 customers lost power across Jefferson County, and the public reported siding damage to homes on College Street in Beaumont.
KBMT-TV reported a funnel cloud west of downtown Beaumont.
The public and KBMT-TV reported a well defined funnel cloud to the west of Bayou Din Golf Course, which was confirmed by photos.
Entergy reported over 1000 customers without power across Jefferson County, particularly in the Labelle and Hillebrandt communities.
Southeast Texas Regional Airport ASOS measured a wind gust of 60 mph.
KBMT-TV reported S MLK Jr. Parkway was closed around Lamar University due to underpass flooding.
Port Arthur Daily News reported large tree branches blown down in Port Arthur.
KFDM-TV reported trees blown down on Carpenter Road.

The public and local media reported the tin metal roof was blown off Snowden Automotive on South MLK Jr. Parkway at Calder Road in downtown Beaumont, injuring one person and damaging several cars in the parking lot.
KFDM-TV reported trees blown down on Helbig Road, with more than 4400 customers losing power in Jefferson County.

An NWS Storm Survey found a low-end EF1 tornado struck the eastern part of Nome. The tornado began southwest of Rodeo Drive in the southeast part of Nome and moved north-northeast, causing minor damage to a rodeo arena. Several outbuildings were then damaged or destroyed on the west side of FM 365 with debris thrown up to 200 yards to the north-northeast. The tornado then entered the Silver Spur Mobile Home Park, where one mobile home had its side sheared off and a nearby RV was flipped over onto a vehicle. The occupants inside were not injured. Another mobile home lost much of its roof, while several other mobile homes suffered various degrees of siding, window, and awning damage…
A Skywarn Spotter reported a funnel cloud on the west side of Beaumont.
KFDM-TV reported penny size hail near Parkdale Mall.

The second winter storm to strike southeast Texas this month brought another round of sleet and snow from the evening hours on February 23rd into the morning hours on February 24th. The heaviest snow accumulations fell across Tyler County, where up to 2.5 inches of snow was reported. Snow accumulations included 2.5 in Rockland, 2.0 in Colmesneil, 2.0 in Chester, 0.5 in Woodville, and trace amounts in Beaumont, Ebenezer, and Orange.

KFDM-TV and the Beaumont Enterprise reported widespread damaged plumbing across Jefferson County due to the record cold temperatures. 10 petrochemical plants and refineries across the county experienced excessive emissions due to cracked pipes, instrument failures, and equipment malfunctions. Entergy reported sporadic power outages through the county. Centerpoint Entergy used trucks to pump natural gas directly into a northwest Beaumont neighborhood of 100 homes after natural gas lines failed due to the cold weather.

A powerful and deep upper level trough of low pressure moved quickly across Texas and Louisiana on Friday, December 4, 2009. At the same time, a strong area of surface low pressure developed in the western Gulf of Mexico. Meanwhile, a cold Arctic airmass filtered southward through the southern United States. All of these factors combined to produce a large area of rain along the Texas coast during the morning hours, which then spread northeastward across southeast Texas during the late morning and afternoon hours. As temperatures gradually cooled, the rain began to mix with and eventually change over to snow from west to east across the area. Snow fell for many hours across much of…
KFDM-TV and the public reported widespread street flooding in downtown Beaumont and Port Arthur.
Port Arthur News reported several streets throughout the city were flooded including Ninth Street.

KBMT-TV and KFDM-TV reported major flash flooding across the city of Beaumont. 3 cars were flooded with water up to the car door windows on the East Tex Freeway at Lucas St. 15 people were rescued from cars stranded in flood waters throughout the city.
A Jefferson County DD6 Mesonet Station measured 4.29 inches of rainfall in approximately 3 hours.
Southeast Texas Regional Airport ASOS measured a wind gust of 54 mph. The public reported a tree blown down near the airport.
KFDM-TV reported strong winds caused the roof collapse of a clothing store on Washington Blvd. in south Beaumont.

Widespread street flooding occurred across the city of Beaumont due to intense rainfall rates. Drainage District 6 Gauges reported 2.05 inches of rain fell between 11am and 12pm with rainfall totals in downtown Beaumont as high as 2.6 inches.

An EF1 Tornado touched down just west of the Kohls Department Store in the Parkdale Mall area. The tornado struck the Kohls, tearing off part of its roof and collapsing the front entrance. Damage to the store forced it to close for several weeks. The tornado continued to the northeast and crossed a Walmart parking lot, flipping over four vehicles and damaging dozens of others. Further to the northeast, the tornado struck Parkdale Mall, damaging the roofs of several department stores. The tornado lifted in the east parking lot of Parkdale Mall before reaching Highway 69. Numerous photographs and videos of the tornado were taken.

All local media reported eight construction workers repairing the roof of a modular home on Bufford Street in Sabine Pass were struck by lightning and injured. One of the workers was critically injured and later died. The home was also set on fire by the lightning strike.
Beaumont Enterprise reported numerous downed powerlines across Beaumont, with 5700 customers without power across the city and 11000 customers without power throughout southeast Texas.
A trained spotter estimated 65 mph winds in Port Arthur.
The KBPT ASOS measured a wind gust of 73 mph from a localized microburst. No damage was reported at the Southeast Texas Regional Airport.

Jefferson County Sheriff Office and the public reported flash flooding across Nederland and Port Arthur. The intersection of Highway 69 and Highway 365 was flooded, and cars were stalled on Jimmy Johnson Boulevard due to high water.

KFDM-TV and the public reported widespread flash flooding across central and eastern Jefferson County. Several major roadways were underwater in the Fannett and Labelle areas. Numerous roadways and underpasses were flooded in Beaumont, including the intersection of Madison Road and Irving Street. Cars were stalled and submerged in floodwaters on Jimmy Johnson Boulevard between Highway 347 and 9th Avenue in Port Arthur.
A Jefferson County DD6 mesonet gauge located 1 mile east-northeast of Fannett measured a three-hour rainfall total of 5.12 inches.
A Jefferson County DD6 Mesonet gauge located 2 miles west of Hamshire measured a three-hour rainfall total of 5.28 inches.
A Jefferson County DD6 mesonet gauge located 1 mile east-northeast of Hamshire measured a six-hour rainfall total of 5.04 inches.
A Jefferson County DD6 Mesonet gauge located 2 miles west of Hamshire measured a six-hour rainfall total of 5.71 inches.
A Jefferson County DD6 mesonet gauge located 1 mile east-northeast of Fannett measured a six-hour rainfall total of 5.43 inches.
A Beaumont TV station reported ping pong ball size hail in Bevil Oaks.
A Beaumont TV station reported nickel size hail in Bevil Oaks.
An industrial plant along the Neches River ESE of Beaumont reported penny size hail.
Power lines blown down near Highway 105 and Major Drive. Reported by TV station in Beaumont.

Five to seven inches of rain fell over a five hour period during the afternoon hours across northern Jefferson County. Widespread flooding of roadways was reported by the public and law enforcement in and around Beaumont. The public reported about a foot of water on Major Drive at Willow Creek Drive in southwest Beaumont, with water covering the yards of area residences. An NWS employee observed flooding on the frontage roads along Interstate 10 at the Highway 69 interchange, and law enforcement reported several of the underpasses in the city were also flooded.

A cold upper level low pressure system moved across Southeast Texas late on December 10, 2008 into the morning hours of December 11, 2008. As cold air aloft associated with this system interacted with widespread rainfall ongoing over the area, precipitation began mixing with sleet and snow, and eventually changed over to all snow in many locations. This rare snow event lasted from 5 to 7 hours, with numerous reports of large snowflakes to the size of half dollars, along with a few reports of thundersnow. Snow totals ranged from a trace or less across far northern areas of southeast Texas and along the coast, to over 5 inches in western Hardin and Jefferson counties. Snow totals acr…
Hurricane Ike caused category 1 wind damage across Jefferson County. Many trees and power lines were downed, some landing on homes and businesses.

A 14-15 storm surge at Sabine Pass resulted in the highest water level ever recorded at that location. Any home that was not elevated was destroyed. The storm surge did not top the seawall in Port Arthur, but wave action on top of the surge did. At least 100 homes were flooded in Port Arthur. The surge also backed up Hillebrandt and Taylor Bayou west of Port Arthur, causing widespread flooding in the Hillebrandt, Hamshire, and Fannett communities. The surge also backed up the Neches River in Beaumont, where some homes along the river flooded. In total, at least 4000 homes were flooded county-wide.

Tropical Storm Edouard produced minor wind damage and some coastal flooding along the southeast Texas coast before it made landfall around 7 am CDT near McFaddin Wildlife Refuge in Jefferson County, TX. The lowest pressure reading in southeast Texas occurred at Sea Rim State Park, where the barometer dropped to 996.6 mb. The strongest wind gusts were mainly 50 to 70 mph across Jefferson and Orange counties, including 49 kt (56 mph) at Southeast Texas Regional Airport ASOS and 62 kt (71 mph) at Texas Point TCOON gage. Rainfall totals were between 1 and 3 inches. The highest storm tides were between 2 and 5 ft MLLW, including 3.75 ft at Sabine Pass North and 4.66 ft at Texas Point. I…
Trees and power lines were blown down in Nederland.
Power lines were blown down near Lamar University.
A 58 mph wind gust was record at the Sabine Pass North station.
In response to an upper level disturbance, severe storms developed across southeast Texas, producing large hail and damaging winds.
As a cold front moved across the region, thunderstorms briefly became severe and produced large hail.
Large hail was reported in thunderstorms across southeast Texas.

Hurricane Humberto made landfall around 1 am in rural southwestern Jefferson County, in McFaddin National Wildlife Refuge. The minimum pressure was estimated to be around 985 mb. While maximum winds were estimated to be 80 knots or 90 mph, hurricane-force winds were confined to a 15 mile wide area. Cities that saw the highest winds of 60 to 80 mph include Port Arthur, Sabine Pass, and Nederland. Damage was primarily trees blown down, roof damage, and power lines downed. At least 12 injuries were reported, due to snake bites, cuts and bruises, and a few broken bones. Power outages occurred to over 100,000 customers. Most urban locations had power back up within a few days, but some…
Heavy rain associated with Hurricane Humberto caused water to enter some homes near Fannett, and also close some service roads along I-10 in the Beuamont area.
A 25 year old man was killed when lightning struck him. He was working on a barge near the Motiva Port Arthur dock.
A roof was blown off an auto sales company on Fannett Road at Highway 69.
Jefferson County Sheriff Office reported a power pole blown down east of China.
Some secondary roads were closed in the Hamshire area due to heavy rains.
A funnel cloud was seen near Groves, over the marshes, but causing no damage.
Isolated severe thunderstorm produced large hail in Jefferson and Orange County.
Lamar University recorded 69 mph wind gust.
Highway 105 between Bevil Oaks and Sour Lake was under water after three to five inches of rain.
Residential streets had 2-3 feet of water on them and were impassable.
Feeder roads on Interstate 10 near Beaumont were closed due to high water. Cars were stranded in the deep water.
Several underpasses were closed in Beaumont due to high water.
A tornado destroyed 5 mobile homes and damaged an additional 20 homes just east of China. Trees and power lines were blown down.

Tides ran high on October 16th as a strong pressure gradient caused abnormally strong winds along the coast. The NOS tide gage at Sabine Pass recorded tides running 2 feet above normal. It reached its highest level of 4.2 MLLW.
Underpasses were barricaded after five inches of rain fell in a short period of time.
Several cars were damaged when they drove into flooded underpasses.
A tree was blown down on Craigen Road. Numerous power lines were also downed.

Water entered as many as 30 homes in the the Fannett area, where as much as 17 inches of rain had fallen. A 13 year old boy in Beaumont drowned after he was electrocuted in his back yard by a downed power line and fell in standing water.
Police report cars totally submerged under overpasses. People had to swim from their vehicles.
Many underpasses were flooded and impassable. Corley Avenue in South Beaumont was flooded.
An old rice dryer was wrapped around a utility pole. A small building was moved 2 feet off its blocks.
C-MAN site at Sea Rim State Park recorded a 64 mph wind gust.

Although Hurricane Rita made landfall just east of the Texas - Louisiana border, she moved northwest and moved across southeast Texas in the morning hours of September 24th as a dangerous category 3 hurricane with sustained winds of 120 mph. Along the coast of Jefferson County, storm surges near 10 feet occurred near Sabine Pass, where over 90 percent of the homes were severely damaged or destroyed. The storm surge backed up the Sabine River, and flooded a small section of downtown Orange with around 4 to 5 feet of storm surge. Winds blew over 100 mph across the entire region, snapping and uprooting trees, and damaged over 125,000 homes and businesses. Some homes in rural Jasper an…
Trees were blown down.
Weather equipment recorded 62 mph wind gust.
Weather equipment recorded 57 mph wind gust.
Trees and power lines were blown down.
Numerous trees and power lines were down throughout the city. Over 11,000 customers lost power.
Trees were blown down.
Heavy rains caused flood waters to enter one home in Nederland.
Nearly 4 inches of rain on already saturated grounds caused significant urban flooding, resulting in several stalled vehicles.
Water was entering a garage due to high water.
Several streets were impassable due to high water.
Several homes received roof damage due to uprooted trees falling on them in the Pinewood subdivision.
A small tornado touched down briefly in Beaumont, damaging the overhead door of a business and several cars in the parking lot.
Homes and streets in Port Neches were flooded when around 5 to 6 inches of rain fell in less than 2 hours.

Around 6 to 8 inches of rain fell in less than 2 hours, causing significant flooding to sections of Beaumont. Water entered homes, vehicles were left stranded on the roads, but fortunately no injuries or deaths were reported.

As much as six to seven inches of rain fell in less than six hours, resulting in flooding of area roads in Jefferson and Orange Counties. Bridge City and Vidor were among the locations in Orange County where roads were closed off due to floodwaters.
Around seven inches of rain fell in less than 6 hours, resulting in flash flooding across sections of Beaumont. Several homes near Roy Guess Elementary School had water enter them.
Trees and power lines were blown down.
SKYWARN spotter reported trees and power lines down.
Several homes were flooded in Port Arthur as a result of excessive rain over a two day period.

Over 400 homes were flooded across Jefferson County. At least 200 of these homes had at least 6 inches of water. This was the result of five inches of rain in less than four hours on top of already saturated grounds.
Trees were blown down across Highway 73.

Between 6 and 8 inches of rain fell in less than 6 hours. Water filled up in underpasses up to 8 feet deep. A woman drove her car into the deep water, and drowned. A hospital had the emergency room floor flooded. Over 500 homes in Beaumont had water enter them.
A utility company reported trees were blown down on power lines along Highway 69.
Several trees were blown down.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down.
Over seven inches of rain fell in less than 24 hours, resulting in street flooding and minor flooding of garages in Nederland and Port Arthur.

High winds associated with a severe thunderstorm blew down numerous trees and power lines. The most significant damage was to the Groves Middle School, where the gymnasium lost part of its roof and one wall.
Between three and six inches of rain fell in a few hours, resulting in street flooding of the Orange and Beaumont areas.
Several trees were blown down, damaging a trailer and barn.
After 8 to 10 inches of rain, several roads flooded and were closed.
A local TV station mesonet weather site recorded a 61 mph wind gust during a thunderstorm.
A tornado touched down near Cardinal Drive and damage several warehouses and businesses, before hitting a school gym.
The tornado that originated in Hardin County dissipated in rural sections of Jefferson County, and was seen by several motorists. It caused little, if any, damage.
A barn and trailer were damaged during a severe thunderstorm.
An additional two to three inches of rain resulted in extended flooding from Nome and China to Port Arthur. The primary damage was to roads and property.
Between five and eight inches of rain resulted in major street flooding in urban areas of Jefferson County, damaging several roads.

Around ten inches of rain fell in less than six hours, resulting in widespread flooding across northern Jefferson County, including the metropolitan area of Beaumont. Many people awoke to see flood waters in their homes, vehicles, and businesses. Nearly 900 homes were damaged, but only 10 were classified as destroyed. Roads and bridges also received some damage from the flood waters.

Tropical Storm Allison caused minor problems along coastal sections of southeast Texas, but eventually resulted in catstrophic flood losses further inland. Wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph resulted in minor roof damage to less than ten homes along the coast in Jefferson County between the evening of June 5th and the early morning hours of June 6th. A two foot storm surge resulted in minor beach erosion and portions of Highway 82 between Sabine Pass and Port Arthur to go under water during high tide during the nighttime high tide of June 5th to 6th. The specific flood events that occurred between June 7th and 9th were a result of the remnants of Tropical Storm Allison, as it meandered acr…
Numerous trees and power lines were downed.
Trees and power lines were downed across the city during a severe thunderstorm.
SAWRS observation recorded 72 mph winds during a thunderstorm.
Fire department reported trees blown down, and roof damage to one home after a severe thunderstorm passed through Nome.

High winds estimated between 40 and 60 mph blew down many trees and power lines across southeast Texas. Trees were knocked onto homes and vehicles in Beaumont, Port Arthur and Nederland in Jefferson County. In Mauriceville in Orange County, high winds toppled trees onto the train tracks. The high winds were a result of a strong high pressure system over the area.
Sheriff department reported trees blown down.
Police reported trees blown down.
Utility poles were blown down, as well as several trees.
Trees and power lines downed in Bevil Oaks.

Between 5 and 7.5 inches of rain fell in less than three hours, resulting in significant flooding of central Jefferson County. The hardest hit area was Nederland, where several homes and businesses, including a hotel, had over a foot of water enter them. There were many reports of stalled cars on feeder roads off of Highway 69.
A roof was blown off a home in 60 mph winds.

The Groves Middle School received the brunt of the second tornado to hit Jefferson County this morning. The roof of the gymnasium was torn off, water damaged the interior, and a brick wall was blown down. Three classrooms were damaged from broken glass. Over a dozen neighboring homes in the 5000 block of Cleveland Avenue received damage. Two of these were severe, when trees fell on the homes. Many trees and power lines were blown down.
65 mph winds were recorded at a local oil refinery.

One man was injured when his mobile home flipped over as a tornado passed nearby. Three other people in the home were uninjured. The home rolled at least 25 yards into the woods behind the home. This mobile home was tied down, but the tie downs either snapped or were pulled out of the ground. Debris from this home was scattered over a mile east on Highway 73. A total of two mobile homes were destroyed and another one was severely damaged. Many trees and power lines were downed along Highway 73.
Trees, power lines, and a billboard were blown down across Beaumont.
Roof was blown off a building, landing on a tractor trailer truck and crushing it. Numerous trees were blown down.

A microburst cut a 2 mile long path of damage through Groves. The worst damage occurred to a church, which lost part of the roof and one wall. Other homes in the area received minor damage, such as lost shingles.
A 33 year old woman was struck by lightning as she was taking down a picnic umbrella in front of her house. She received minor injuries.
Several trees and power lines were blown down.
Trees and power lines downed.
Hail damaged several cars in the Port Arthur area.

A strong squall line caused wind gusts in excess of 60 mph, downing many trees and power lines across the Beaumont region. Some homes and businesses were damaged when trees fell on them. On Delaware Street, trees were either split, uprooted, or ripped apart, littering the street and yards. Two school buses were hit by falling trees, but no injuries were reported.

A strong tornado that developed in Liberty County moved into western Jefferson County, destroying several rice dryers, two mobile homes, and a brick house. Five people were injured in the mobile homes and brick house. Two people received broken necks and other injuries after they were ejected from one of the mobile homes.A fiberglass tub from the destroyed brick home was found one mile away. Cancelled checks and other paperwork were found seven miles away in southern Hardin County.This tornado was strongest southwest of Nome, and was weakening as it passed through the small community of Nome. At least 20 homes received minor damage such as shingles blown off, and many trees were blown down.
SKYWARN spotters reported numerous streets flooded across the Beaumont area. Rain totals were between 2.5 and 3.5 inches in 2 hours.
Over 10 inches of rain, combined with high water levels in the marshes, resulted in several homes being flooded in Hampshire, Fannett, and LaBelle. Water covered area roadways for several hours.

Significant flooding occurred in Beaumont when as much as 5 inches of rain fell in less than 2 hours. Many streets had as much as two feet of water over them, and passing vehicles caused wakes that would crash into the buildings.

Tropical Storm Frances was the third tropical system to impact southeast Texas in 3 weeks, and caused the worst damage. Wind gusts in excess of 50 mph occurred along the coast on September 11th, but most of the damage occurred from the high tides. At Sabine Pass, the tide reading reached 5.3 ft MSL, which was one of the highest tides in the last 30 years. On top of the high tides, heavy rain lasting several days dropped 8 to 10 inches of rain across the region.At Sea Rim State Park, water got to the top of the dunes, which is 8 to 9 feet higher than normal.Offshore oil workers evacuated before 70 to 80 mph wind gusts impacted the rigs offshore. Many of these evacuees landed in Sabi…
Hurricane Earl passed well to the east of southeast Texas, but high tide readings of 3.5 ft MSL caused minor flooding along the coast of Jefferson County, primarily in the Sabine Pass area.
Numerous trees and power lines downed in Beaumont. Several carports were blown down.

Tropical Storm Charley did some damage across Jefferson County's coastal areas. Wind gusts were estimated between 30 and 40 knots at the height of the storm, and as much as six inches of rain fell around rural sections of Jefferson County.At Sabine Pass, minor beach erosion occurred between Sabine and Sea Rim State Park. Coastal flooding destroyed the access road behind the Sabine Pass Pilots House. Highway 87 between Sabine Pass and Port Arthur had around one foot of water across it in two places during high tide.No evacuations were ordered for Jefferson County, and no deaths or injuries were reported.

Between three and five inches of rain fell in less than one hour across Jefferson and Orange Counties. Several roads were impassable, including many streets near Interstate 10. Two to three feet of water was reported across many streets.
Two men were in a house under construction when a combination of wind and rain caused the collapse of the building. One man was killed, and the other was slightly injured.
A rood was blown off a storage building at Lamar University. Several trees were also blown down in the area.

Trees were blown down across China in western Jefferson County. A home under construction was leveled due to the estimated 60 mph winds. Houses and barns next door were not damaged. The China Elementary School had parts of its roof torn off, and debris from the roof went through the windows of a classroom. No injuries were reported.
Sheet metal was ripped from several buildings, and power lines were downed in a one block area on Gulfway Drive in Port Arthur.
Tug boat operator recorded wind gust of 58 mph.
58 mph wind gust recorded at Huntsman Plant.
Trees blown down in Nederland.
Winds recorded as 66 mph near the petroleum industry plants in the Port Arthur area.
The roof was blown off a local restaurant during a severe thunderstorm.
Around five inches of rain fell in less than three hours, resulting in several streets to be flooded in Nederland and Port Arthur.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew down several utility poles and wires in Nederland. At 5:00 am, an 18 wheeler was blown off I-10 five miles west of Beaumont. The driver received minor injuries.

A slow moving cold front stalled across the Golden Traingle region, producing between six and nine inches of rain in some places. The hardest hit areas included Bridge City and Port Arthur, where streets were flooded for several hours. A number of automobile wrecks occurred in the rain, due to slick roadways. Injuries were mostly minor.
Several trees and power lines were downed during a severe thunderstorm.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew several trees and power lines down.
Around three inches of rain fell in less than one hour, resulting in street flooding in Port Arthur and Groves.

A small tornado formed along a thunderstorm outflow, tearing through the Chevron Oil Plant. Three men received minor bumps and scrapes when hit by debris from the tornado. The tornado move east to west, and dissipated in the bayous behind the plant. Severe thunderstorm winds that preced the tornado also blew throughout the city of Port Arthur, resulting in numerous trees and power lines down.
Several trees were blown down near China.

A record ice storm paralyzed southeast Texas and southwest Louisiana. Around 90,000 electric customers across southeast Texas were without power for up to six days. Emergency shelters were opended for several nights due to the cold weather following the ice storm. More trees and power lines were knocked down in this ice storm than what came down during Hurricane Bonnie in 1986. Hundreds of homes received minor damage due to trees or tree limbs falling on roofs. Several house fires were directly or indirectly related to the ice storm, but fortunately there were only no injuries. Numerous traffic accidents attributed to icy roads led to several minor injuries. One death was indirectl…

Nearly nine inches of rain fell in eight hours across the Beaumont-Port Arthur region, resulting in numerous road closures. Over 100 homes and businesses had 6 inches to two feet of water in them. During the morning rush hour, over 100 cars were abandoned in rising waters.
As many as 9,000 lightning strikes this evening resulted in one man injured, one house fire, and several telephone poles damaged.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down 5 miles northwest of Beaumont.
Several trees were blown down in the Bevil Oaks area.
Strong winds behind a cold front knocked power lines down and caused 1 TV station to be off the air.
Record cold temperatures caused numerous water pipes to burst, especially in Port Arthur.
Several streets and underpasses were impassable due to high water.
Groves and Port Neches Fire Department officials witnessed a small tornado touch down twice in the marshes of Port Neches and Groves. No damage occurred.
Trees blown down across the city.
Wind gust reported at Jefferson County Airport.
Thunderstorms in the area produced dime-size hail on Highway 69 north of Beaumont.
Port Arthur police report trees and power lines down along Highway 87.
Department of Public Safety officers report power lines down and street signs blown over.
Department of Public Safety officers report power lines down and street signs blown over.
Department of Public Safety officers report power lines down and street signs blown over.

An National Weather Service employee spotted a tornado between one-half and two miles west of the Jefferson County Airport moving to the northeast at 30 mph. This tornado was in sight for about five minutes before being blocked by heavy rainfall. No damage was noted.

Beaumont Emergency Management reported intermittent hail through the county of diameter up to three-quarters inch. The National Weather Service office observed hail one-half of an inch and possibly larger.

Trees were knocked down in western Beaumont and in Groves. In Port Arthur, a microburst produced wind gusts estimated at 70+ mph. It caused structural damage to some buildings, broke many windows, and knocked numerous trees. The storm path was 200 yards wide and 2 miles long. Two people were slightly injured by flying glass.

Trees were knocked down in western Beaumont and in Groves. In Port Arthur, a microburst produced wind gusts estimated at 70+ mph. It caused structural damage to some buildings, broke many windows, and knocked numerous trees. The storm path was 200 yards wide and 2 miles long. Two people were slightly injured by flying glass.

Trees were knocked down in western Beaumont and in Groves. In Port Arthur, a microburst produced wind gusts estimated at 70+ mph. It caused structural damage to some buildings, broke many windows, and knocked numerous trees. The storm path was 200 yards wide and 2 miles long. Two people were slightly injured by flying glass.
Numerous trees down in the western part of the county reported by sheriff.

A small tornado was observed by National Weather Service personnel 2 miles southwest of the Jefferson County Airport. It damaged several telephone poles as it moved to the northeast. It took a roof off a barn at Port Acres 4 miles southwest of the airport before dissipating.
,An isolated gust was reported in a thunderstorm at the National Weather Service Office.
A wind gust to 51 knot was recorded at the Beaumont-Port Arthur Weather Office.
A severe thunderstorm struck Beaumont shortly after 0330 CST, producing damaging winds that uprooted trees in the northern part of the city.
The Port Arthur Police Department reported dime-size hail in downtown.
